title: 63-item medical leadership competencies questionnaire (adapted from Wagner et al by Çitaku et al)
description: A 63-item questionnaire assessing perceived importance of medical leadership competencies, adapted by Çitaku et al from a 107-item LC scale developed by Wagner et al to be more relevant to medical education. This study applied it to Latin American physician-leaders, grouping the 63 questions into 5 major categories (task management, self-management, social responsibility, innovation, and leading others) and analyzing the proportion of respondents rating each competency 4 or 5. Internal consistency reliability was computed (Cronbach's α = .830294).
requirements: Respondents must hold an ongoing leadership position, per the survey's introductory instruction
constraints: The article notes the survey was not translated to the physicians' native languages, which could be detrimental because it deals with relatively abstract concepts
target_learners: physicians in oncology and related areas holding leadership positions
target_learning_goals: perceived importance of medical leadership competencies across five domains
examples: Sent to nearly 8,000 physicians of participating Latin American professional organizations via SurveyMonkey and institutional e-mail, collecting 217 responses
